trigger.body_text: MACHINIST.IN » Sansera Engineering Invests in Expansion Including Land Near Bengaluru and New Forging Facility Sansera Engineering Limited, a manufacturer of precision-engineered components, has reported a capital expenditure of INR 5,911 million in FY25, with key investments directed toward the acquisition of land near Bengaluru, the purchase of a facility in Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, and the installation of new plant and equipment, including a forging facility and press at one of its existing sites. The new capital projects are part of Sansera’s strategy to strengthen its operational footprint and support business across both automotive and non-automotive segments. Sansera’s order book stood at INR 18,511 million as of March 31, 2025, with 28 percent of new orders in FY25 coming from the aerospace, defence, and semiconductor (ADS) segment. trigger.body_text: Lumax Auto Technologies Stock Near Record High; 3 Key Things Investors Should Know Before Investing Advertisment Auto ancillary stocks have had a good run lately, and one name trading close to its all time high is now backing that up with real numbers. Strong festive demand, a shift toward smarter vehicle parts, and steady cost control have all come together in one quarter. But is the rally justified, or is the stock running ahead of the fundamentals? Let's dig into the details. Advertisment Lumax Auto Technologies Ltd is currently trading at ₹1,969, down 1.07% or ₹19.15 from its previous close of ₹1,990. It touched its 52 week high of ₹2,149 on 1st of September 2026 and in last one year the stock has jumped close to 50%. The company commands a market capitalisation of ₹13,419 crore , with the stock trading at a consolidated price to earnings ratio of 35 times.  Financial Snapshot Lumax Auto Technologies kicked off FY27 on a strong footing. Revenue for the June quarter came in at ₹1,364 crore, up 33% year on year. EBITDA grew even faster, rising 51% to ₹205 crore, with margins expanding by 190 basis points to 15.1%. Profit after tax stood at ₹99 crore, up a sharp 83% compared to the same quarter last year. The company managed this margin expansion despite plastics, its biggest raw material, getting costlier by 30-40% this quarter. Management says most of this cost gets passed on to OEMs within the same quarter itself, thanks to back to back pricing arrangements, and that's really what protected the bottom line here. Advertisment A Shift Toward Smarter, Connected Auto Parts The company isn't just making plastic components and lighting anymore. It's now building sensors, telematics units, antennas, and something called a Body Control Module, which is basically the brain that controls a lot of electronic functions in a car. This is part of a broader industry shift, where vehicles are moving from being purely mechanical machines to intelligent, connected ones. Around 22 new sub product categories are reportedly in the pipeline, either in proof of concept stage or under active development with customers. The idea is simple, these newer tech products usually carry fatter margins than plain old plastic parts, and the order book already shows 25-30% coming from these newer technologies. Order Book Gives Multi Year Visibility The company is sitting on an order book worth ₹1,600 crore, which is a decent cushion for future revenue. About 24% of this is expected to be executed within the current financial year itself, with 56% spilling into FY28 and the rest into FY29. Advertisment Advanced Plastics continues to be the largest contributor to this order book, but the Mechatronics division, which houses all the newer tech products, is quietly building a strong pipeline too, currently sitting around ₹400-500 crore. New Customer Wins and Capacity Expansion Greenfuel Energy, the company's CNG business, just onboarded a large passenger vehicle maker as a fresh customer for its CNG delivery systems. To support this, a new facility is coming up in one of the western states. Meanwhile, a mega plant is being built to consolidate four separate joint ventures under one roof, aimed at cutting fixed costs and improving efficiency. Capex for the quarter stood at ₹23 crore, and the full year guidance remains at around ₹300 crore, funded mostly through internal accruals rather than fresh debt. Bottom Line The numbers here genuinely look encouraging, revenue growth, margin expansion, and profit growth are all moving in the same direction, which doesn't happen too often. The order book gives decent visibility for the next couple of years, and the company's push into smarter, connected auto parts could open up a new growth avenue if it plays out well.  That said, management itself has flagged that growth rates could slow down in the coming quarters simply because last year's base got unusually high after GST rationalization kicked in. trigger.body_text: MACHINIST.IN » Ramkrishna Forgings commissions 8,000-ton hot forging press line in Jharkhand Ramkrishna Forgings Limited has commenced commercial production from an 8,000-ton hot forging press line at its Plant V manufacturing facility in Baliguma, Saraikela-Kharswan district, Jharkhand. The line adds an installed forging capacity of 40,000 tonnes per annum and became operational on 06 March 2026. The company said that the addition increases its total forging production capacity, including aluminium forging, to 311,400 tonnes per annum. The capacity expansion forms part of the company’s manufacturing operations at Plant V. Prior to the expansion, Ramkrishna Forgings reported existing forging capacity of 268,400 tonnes per annum across hot, warm and cold forging operations. The company’s capacity utilisation stood at 73.20 percent as of 31 December 2025. The investment required for the new press line was INR 800 million. The company said the project was financed through a mix of debt and internal accruals. The 8,000-ton press line is intended to increase the company’s hot forging output by 40,000 tonnes per annum. Ramkrishna Forgings Limited is a manufacturer of forged components used in automotive and industrial applications and operates multiple forging facilities in India. trigger.title: Deccan Gold Mines invests in Spanish tungsten project, expands critical minerals footprint
trigger.evidence_quote: Deccan Gold Mines invests in Spanish tungsten project, expands critical minerals footprint Saturday, September 12, 2026 Advertise with us News SEARCH NEWS --> NEWS HOME � BUSI
trigger.body_text: Deccan Gold Mines invests in Spanish tungsten project, expands critical minerals footprint Saturday, September 12, 2026 Advertise with us News SEARCH NEWS --> NEWS HOME � BUSINESS Deccan Gold Mines invests in Spanish tungsten project, expands critical minerals footprint Share Tweet    -->       COMMENT Mumbai (Maharashtra) | December 23, 2025 7:18:53 PM IST Deccan Gold Mines has announced a strategic investment in a tungsten exploration project in Spain, marking the company's entry into a critical minerals asset in Europe amid tightening global supply conditions. The Bengaluru-and Mumbai-based company said it has acquired an initial stake in the Logrosan tungsten project in western Spain, with an option to increase its ownership to up to 75 per cent before production commences. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Deccan Gold Mines said the investment aligns with its long-term strategy to build a diversified international portfolio focused on minerals essential to modern industrial economies. Logrosan is an early-stage exploration asset located in a mineral-rich region with known occurrences of tungsten, tin, rare earth elements and gold. Deccan Gold said ongoing exploration and drilling could allow the conversion of existing mineralisation into defined mineral resources within one to two years, subject to technical studies and regulatory approvals. Spain has emerged as a strategic destination for critical minerals in Europe, supported by a favourable conditions, competitive operating costs, established infrastructure and proximity to industrial markets. The country also does not levy production-based mining royalties, a factor that has drawn growing interest as Europe seeks to secure diversified supply chains for strategic raw materials. Tungsten is classified as a critical mineral by major economies due to its use in defence, aerospace, cutting tools, electronics and high-temperature alloys. More than 80% of global tungsten supply is currently dominated by China, heightening concerns over supply security and increasing demand for alternative sources. "Our entry into the Logrosan tungsten project reflects Deccan Gold's long-term vision of building a globally relevant portfolio in minerals that are critical to modern economies," Managing Director Hanuma Prasad Modali said, according to a release. "Tungsten sits at the intersection of national security, advanced manufacturing and industrial resilience." Early exploration and limited drilling at Logrosan have produced encouraging results, including intersections of 3 metres at 0.42% tungsten trioxide (WO) and 8 metres at 0.32% WO. Isolated high-grade gold intercepts, including 1 metre at 96.2 grams per tonne, have also been reported. Deccan Gold said the broader region offers potential upside from associated gold and rare earth element targets, including the nearby Maria Gold Project. Maria is considered a prospective near-surface gold and antimony system, with historical work and recent sampling identifying gold anomalies. The company added that its technical expertise in gold exploration and resource evaluation is transferable to tungsten systems, given similarities in geological settings and mineralisation styles. Deccan Gold Mines holds exploration assets across India and overseas, including projects in Mozambique, Kyrgyzstan, Finland and Spain, and is positioning itself to benefit from rising global demand for critical minerals. trigger.body_text: Lumax Auto Technologies Stock Near Record High; 3 Key Things Investors Should Know Before Investing Advertisment Auto ancillary stocks have had a good run lately, and one name trading close to its all time high is now backing that up with real numbers. Strong festive demand, a shift toward smarter vehicle parts, and steady cost control have all come together in one quarter. But is the rally justified, or is the stock running ahead of the fundamentals? Let's dig into the details. Advertisment Lumax Auto Technologies Ltd is currently trading at ₹1,969, down 1.07% or ₹19.15 from its previous close of ₹1,990. It touched its 52 week high of ₹2,149 on 1st of September 2026 and in last one year the stock has jumped close to 50%. The company commands a market capitalisation of ₹13,419 crore , with the stock trading at a consolidated price to earnings ratio of 35 times.  Financial Snapshot Lumax Auto Technologies kicked off FY27 on a strong footing. Revenue for the June quarter came in at ₹1,364 crore, up 33% year on year. EBITDA grew even faster, rising 51% to ₹205 crore, with margins expanding by 190 basis points to 15.1%. Profit after tax stood at ₹99 crore, up a sharp 83% compared to the same quarter last year. The company managed this margin expansion despite plastics, its biggest raw material, getting costlier by 30-40% this quarter. Management says most of this cost gets passed on to OEMs within the same quarter itself, thanks to back to back pricing arrangements, and that's really what protected the bottom line here. Advertisment A Shift Toward Smarter, Connected Auto Parts The company isn't just making plastic components and lighting anymore. It's now building sensors, telematics units, antennas, and something called a Body Control Module, which is basically the brain that controls a lot of electronic functions in a car. This is part of a broader industry shift, where vehicles are moving from being purely mechanical machines to intelligent, connected ones. Around 22 new sub product categories are reportedly in the pipeline, either in proof of concept stage or under active development with customers. The idea is simple, these newer tech products usually carry fatter margins than plain old plastic parts, and the order book already shows 25-30% coming from these newer technologies. Order Book Gives Multi Year Visibility The company is sitting on an order book worth ₹1,600 crore, which is a decent cushion for future revenue. About 24% of this is expected to be executed within the current financial year itself, with 56% spilling into FY28 and the rest into FY29. Advertisment Advanced Plastics continues to be the largest contributor to this order book, but the Mechatronics division, which houses all the newer tech products, is quietly building a strong pipeline too, currently sitting around ₹400-500 crore. New Customer Wins and Capacity Expansion Greenfuel Energy, the company's CNG business, just onboarded a large passenger vehicle maker as a fresh customer for its CNG delivery systems. To support this, a new facility is coming up in one of the western states. Meanwhile, a mega plant is being built to consolidate four separate joint ventures under one roof, aimed at cutting fixed costs and improving efficiency. Capex for the quarter stood at ₹23 crore, and the full year guidance remains at around ₹300 crore, funded mostly through internal accruals rather than fresh debt. Bottom Line The numbers here genuinely look encouraging, revenue growth, margin expansion, and profit growth are all moving in the same direction, which doesn't happen too often. The order book gives decent visibility for the next couple of years, and the company's push into smarter, connected auto parts could open up a new growth avenue if it plays out well.  That said, management itself has flagged that growth rates could slow down in the coming quarters simply because last year's base got unusually high after GST rationalization kicked in. India’s structural advantages make it a strategically well-positioned location for establishing a sorbitol production facility. The country’s large starch processing industry  particularly glucose syrup manufacturing operations in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat provides investors with direct, cost-competitive access to the primary raw material, reducing import dependency and inbound logistics costs relative to producers in countries without domestic starch processing infrastructure. trigger.body_text: MACHINIST.IN » Ramkrishna Forgings commissions 8,000-ton hot forging press line in Jharkhand Ramkrishna Forgings Limited has commenced commercial production from an 8,000-ton hot forging press line at its Plant V manufacturing facility in Baliguma, Saraikela-Kharswan district, Jharkhand. The line adds an installed forging capacity of 40,000 tonnes per annum and became operational on 06 March 2026. The company said that the addition increases its total forging production capacity, including aluminium forging, to 311,400 tonnes per annum. The capacity expansion forms part of the company’s manufacturing operations at Plant V. Prior to the expansion, Ramkrishna Forgings reported existing forging capacity of 268,400 tonnes per annum across hot, warm and cold forging operations. The company’s capacity utilisation stood at 73.20 percent as of 31 December 2025. The investment required for the new press line was INR 800 million. The company said the project was financed through a mix of debt and internal accruals. The 8,000-ton press line is intended to increase the company’s hot forging output by 40,000 tonnes per annum. Ramkrishna Forgings Limited is a manufacturer of forged components used in automotive and industrial applications and operates multiple forging facilities in India. trigger.body_text: Deccan Gold Mines invests in Spanish tungsten project, expands critical minerals footprint Saturday, September 12, 2026 Advertise with us News SEARCH NEWS --> NEWS HOME � BUSINESS Deccan Gold Mines invests in Spanish tungsten project, expands critical minerals footprint Share Tweet    -->       COMMENT Mumbai (Maharashtra) | December 23, 2025 7:18:53 PM IST Deccan Gold Mines has announced a strategic investment in a tungsten exploration project in Spain, marking the company's entry into a critical minerals asset in Europe amid tightening global supply conditions. The Bengaluru-and Mumbai-based company said it has acquired an initial stake in the Logrosan tungsten project in western Spain, with an option to increase its ownership to up to 75 per cent before production commences. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Deccan Gold Mines said the investment aligns with its long-term strategy to build a diversified international portfolio focused on minerals essential to modern industrial economies. Logrosan is an early-stage exploration asset located in a mineral-rich region with known occurrences of tungsten, tin, rare earth elements and gold. Deccan Gold said ongoing exploration and drilling could allow the conversion of existing mineralisation into defined mineral resources within one to two years, subject to technical studies and regulatory approvals. Spain has emerged as a strategic destination for critical minerals in Europe, supported by a favourable conditions, competitive operating costs, established infrastructure and proximity to industrial markets. The country also does not levy production-based mining royalties, a factor that has drawn growing interest as Europe seeks to secure diversified supply chains for strategic raw materials. Tungsten is classified as a critical mineral by major economies due to its use in defence, aerospace, cutting tools, electronics and high-temperature alloys. More than 80% of global tungsten supply is currently dominated by China, heightening concerns over supply security and increasing demand for alternative sources. "Our entry into the Logrosan tungsten project reflects Deccan Gold's long-term vision of building a globally relevant portfolio in minerals that are critical to modern economies," Managing Director Hanuma Prasad Modali said, according to a release. "Tungsten sits at the intersection of national security, advanced manufacturing and industrial resilience." Early exploration and limited drilling at Logrosan have produced encouraging results, including intersections of 3 metres at 0.42% tungsten trioxide (WO) and 8 metres at 0.32% WO. Isolated high-grade gold intercepts, including 1 metre at 96.2 grams per tonne, have also been reported. Deccan Gold said the broader region offers potential upside from associated gold and rare earth element targets, including the nearby Maria Gold Project. Maria is considered a prospective near-surface gold and antimony system, with historical work and recent sampling identifying gold anomalies. The company added that its technical expertise in gold exploration and resource evaluation is transferable to tungsten systems, given similarities in geological settings and mineralisation styles. Deccan Gold Mines holds exploration assets across India and overseas, including projects in Mozambique, Kyrgyzstan, Finland and Spain, and is positioning itself to benefit from rising global demand for critical minerals.
